subject: Mutual action agenda: stage gates, evaluation timeline, and uplift framework
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Claire Tunney <claire@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action agenda: stage gates, evaluation timeline, and uplift framework

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our meeting, I put together a concise mutual-action agenda that ties the evaluation gates to conditional commercial milestones so both teams have visibility on expectations. High level:

- Week 1–3: PoC + preflight (security review, SOC 2 evidence)
- Week 4–6: Integration proof points (latency & cost baselines)
- Week 7–10: Pilot ramp with committed throughput (pricing ladder kicks in at 25%/50%/100% of target)

Attached is the MAP draft (Catalyst_MAP_v3.pdf) and the pricing slate that shows conditional uplift/discounts tied to ramp triggers. The key ask from our side is clarity on the target production QPS and the internal approval window for commit decisions — that will determine which discounts we can offer on ramp.

Next steps I propose:
1) Your procurement/technical sponsor confirms target QPS and data residency constraints by Nov 3.
2) We run the security checklist in parallel (redwood-eval-checklist.docx).
3) If both are green, we agree to a three-stage ramp with explicit uplift milestones and a capped ramp discount schedule to be included in the SOW.

If you like this, I can loop in Ben for approval on the conditional uplift parameters.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
[Attachment: Catalyst_MAP_v3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: pricing_slate_q4.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Claire Tunney <claire@catalysthealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Narang <ravi@catalysthealth.com>, CatalystHealth Procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action agenda: stage gates, evaluation timeline, and uplift framework

Sofia —

Thanks for the tidy plan. A few notes from our side:

- Target production QPS: 1,200 sustained during peak windows; goal is 3,000 burst with graceful degradation.
- We can complete the security checklist by Nov 6 but will need the SOC 2 artifact sent to Ravi (copied).
- Procurement needs to see a firm last-date-to-commit before the ramp starts; can you confirm a cutoff and the exact discount bands tied to each ramp threshold?

On pricing: we are comfortable with a staged commit but we need a two-way uplift guardrail — if we hit the 50% ramp, we expect price protection for six months and a defined path for expansion discounts. Also, any upfront credit or trial credits should be formalized in the SOW.

Happy to align — can we get the exact band percentages and the last-commit-date by EOD Nov 4?

Thanks,
Claire Tunney
Head of Product Operations, CatalystHealth
claire@catalysthealth.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Claire Tunney <claire@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action agenda: stage gates, evaluation timeline, and uplift framework

Claire —

Appreciate the details — they help a lot. Quick answers below and a proposed conditional uplift framework attached.

- Cutoff (last-commit-date): Nov 12, 2026 — commitments after that date move you to the standard enterprise cadence for onboarding and pricing (we want clarity for capacity planning).
- Discount band proposal (conditional on hitting ramp thresholds within 90 days of pilot start):
  * 25% of target throughput: 8% discount on unit price
  * 50% of target throughput: 14% discount + 1 month price protection
  * 100% of target throughput: 20% discount + 3 months price protection and accelerated SLA review

- Trial credit / upfront: we can provide a $15k evaluation credit applied to first invoice if commitment is signed by Nov 12.

Aditya (cc) — can you confirm we can honor the 20% top-tier discount and the evaluation credit in a flexible SOW? Ben — pinging you for executive sign-off on the conditional uplift and the short price-protection window.

Attached: updated pricing_slate_q4.xlsx with the bands and a brief SOW bulleted appendix.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_slate_q4.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action agenda: stage gates, evaluation timeline, and uplift framework — Approval

Team —

I reviewed Sofia's proposed conditional uplift bands and the $15k evaluation credit. Approve moving forward with the following guardrails:

1) Approve the discount bands as listed (8% / 14% / 20%) tied to the 25/50/100 ramp thresholds with the stated price-protection windows.
2) Evaluation credit capped at $15k and applied to first invoice; procurement must acknowledge in SOW.
3) Last-commit-date of Nov 12 stands; post-deadline commits will revert to standard onboarding timelines and pricing.
4) Any material deviation (longer price-protection, larger credits, or permanent custom SLA) requires my approval and Sales Ops sign-off.

Sofia — please capture these terms in the SOW addendum and share the DocuSign link to Catalyst for signature. Marissa/Aditya — assist with a compact SOW appendix and procurement language.

Ben Carter
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
